episodes.171460: A slow moving thunderstorm dropped locally heavy rain over portions of Colorado County leading to localized flash flooding.
episodes.171532: Strong thunderstorms developed near the Michigan border along a frontal boundary during the afternoon and early evening hours on Wednesday (8/24).  The strongest storm produced hail up to nickel size.
episodes.171574: A rogue thunderstorm developed over Western portions of Madison County on the afternoon/evening of the 23rd. The thunderstorm remained nearly stationary for several hours, dumping prolific amounts of rainfall from the Indian Creek river gage West to neighborhoods along Zierdt Road (near Toyota Field/Trash Panda Stadium). Several instances of flash flooding occurred, with a few residents in the Mountain Brook neighborhood unable to leave/get into their houses due to the roadway being flooded with 8-12 of water.
episodes.171890: Afternoon thunderstorms produce a severe wind gust in Charlotte County and a microburst with extensive wind damage near Ybor City in Hillsborough County.
episodes.172135: Cloud buildups from afternoon heating dropped heavy showers over parts of Oahu.  The rain caused ponding on roadways, and small stream and drainage ditch flooding.  No serious injuries or property damage were reported.
episodes.172254: Early morning thunderstorms developed over parts of south central South Dakota. A severe thunderstorm tracked across northern Tripp County, producing some wind gusts around 70 mph.
episodes.172255: A supercell thunderstorm developed over the southern Black Hills and tracked southeast, weakening on the adjacent plains. The storm produced large hail and heavy rain over the area. Other strong thunderstorms produced heavy rain and localized flash flooding over far southwestern South Dakota. Rain amounts of three to four inches were estimated in some areas. In Oglala Lakota County, flash flooding quickly occurred in Porcupine, with water running over roads. In Custer County, Hopkins Flat Road west and northwest of Pringle was washed out.
episodes.172270: An active monsoon season continued to impact Southern California, with multiple days of thunderstorms reported across the mountains from August 22-26. The main hazards were heavy rain and minor debris flows, as well as gusty winds from thunderstorms.
episodes.172436: Severe weather developed over central into parts of western North Dakota in an environment of enhanced instability and marginal deep layer shear. Many crops were damaged as hail combined with strong wind gusts. The strongest reported wind gust was 76 mph in Mountrail County, while the largest hail was one inch in diameter and occurred with several of the storms in Oliver, McLean, and Mountrail counties. Later in the episode, the focus turned towards flash flooding which occurred in Burleigh County, primarily in and around the city of Bismarck. Vehicles were stranded in flood waters to the south of the North Dakota State Capitol Grounds, and in the 7th Street underpass. Storm sewers were overwhelmed, with manhole covers being pushed off and flood waters escaping.
episodes.172840: Storms moved across Minnesota throughout the day on August 24th and increased in strength over southeast Minnesota in the evening. One storm produced a funnel cloud that was sighted north of Canton (Fillmore County).
episodes.173104: A persistent upper low over Washington favored ample moisture transport into the area. Shear was fairly limited throughout, hence wind gusts were the main concern with these storms, along with potential for heavy rain. Small hail was expected, but a few reports of severe level hail were relayed.
episodes.173225: A low pressure system spinning over northern Louisiana and southern Arkansas brought several rounds of showers and thunderstorms producing heavy rain to Mississippi August 24th through 25th. This resulted in widespread flooding of roads, homes, and businesses around the state.
episodes.173416: A stalled frontal boundary that was draped across the local area began to lift north as a warm front. Increased instability and wind shear along this boundary became the focus for numerous showers and thunderstorms. A few thunderstorms within this more conducive environment were able to intensify and produce severe wind gusts in the coastal waters.
episodes.173466: The axis of the Atlantic high pressure was stretched across the Florida peninsula resulting in relatively light flow at the surface. Aloft, broad troughing over the lower Mississippi Valley and ridging over the Bahamas continued southwesterly flow maintaining the anomalously moist airmass over the area, with PWATs near 2.3 inches. The sea breezes developed in the afternoon with showers and storms developing along the boundaries as they shifted inland. The Atlantic/Gulf sea breeze merger occurred along an axis of rich moisture along I-75 in the evening. Slow-moving storms that developed from the merger dumped about 2 inches of rainfall within an hour west of Ocala.
episodes.173485: Thunderstorms moving through Saginaw Bay produced gusts around 35 knots.
episodes.173507: Weak warm air advection into the state allowed for convection the percolate much of the day, but by late afternoon a shortwave made its way into the area and provided the kinematic enhancement needed to strengthen the convection. Still with moderate CAPE and weak shear, there was little to support widespread coverage of strong storms. Only one storm reached severe limits but it dis result in large hail, tree damage from wind gusts, a brief funnel cloud, and a pocket of heavy rain.
episodes.173538: A cold front moved into the region and stalled while a weakness aloft lingered over area. This provided multiple days of rain while soils were already saturated from previous events. Flash flooded resulted from the prolonged rain.
episodes.173543: A weak frontal boundary and associated surface low pressure remained stationary across North-central Louisiana on August 24th. Precipitable water values were on the order of two inches along and south of this boundary. Meanwhile, a weak shortwave trough began to shift southeastward from the Plains into the Four State Region, which served to reinforce the lift along the frontal boundary and resulted in numerous showers and thunderstorms in the early morning hours. Widespread rainfall amounts of 3-4 inches with isolated higher amounts in excess of 6 inches fell across parts of La Salle Parish which resulted in multiple reports of flash flooding.
episodes.173604: A series of thunderstorms dropped heavy rain over steep terrain about 6 to 10 miles east of the East Entrance to Yellowstone National Park. Flash flooding brought mud and dead tree debris down area streams and creeks, causing impacts to local roads and US Hwy 14 (North Fork Highway).
episodes.173633: Isolated storm produced large hail and damaging winds across the northern portions of the Red River Valley on August 23rd.
episodes.173642: A mid-level high pressure was situated across southern Nevada, with the local area under an northeasterly flow regime. At upper-levels, a disturbance moving northward out northern Baja California resulted in a diffluent flow, favorable for vertical ascent. The moisture and instability parameters were conducive to thunderstorm activity with PWATs 1.5+ inches and MLCAPE values ranging between 1500-2500 J/KG. As it is typical in a northeasterly flow regime, thunderstorms first began to develop along the Mogollon Rim early afternoon and then descended into the lower elevations during the mid to late afternoon hours, affecting the Greater Phoenix area and then tracking southwestward, affecting southwestern Arizona through the early evening hours.
episodes.173675: Numerous clusters of thunderstorms initiated over northern Michigan amidst increasing instability and weak forcing early in the afternoon, eventually tracking southeast across the area. One of these clusters produced damaging winds in Beaverton, including a tree being blown down onto a house.
episodes.173696: A very moist (PWATs 2.0+ inches) and unstable (MLCAPE 2000-3000 J/KG) air mass led to a very conducive environment for vigorous thunderstorm activity across portions of southeast California. Thunderstorms first developed across the higher terrain near Joshua Tree National Park as well as across the mountains of Northern Baja California. With the upper-level flow from the west, these thunderstorms moved eastward into Imperial and Riverside counties, moving into the very moist and unstable air mass. Radar estimated rainfall amounts were upwards of 2-3 inches in some areas, with most of the rain falling in less than 2 hours. There were several incidences of flash flooding and wind impacts around the region. The biggest impact of the day was a washout of a section of eastbound lanes along Interstate-10, which is a major throughway for ground traffic between Phoenix, AZ and Los Angeles, CA. This caused major traffic delays and detours.
episodes.173700: A very moist (PWATs 2.0+ inches) and unstable (MLCAPE 2000-3000 J/KG) air mass led to be a very conducive environment for vigorous thunderstorm activity across portions of southwest Arizona. A cluster of thunderstorms developed near Yuma during the mid-afternoon hours leading to flash flooding and damaging winds across the Fortuna Hills area. Thereafter, additional storm complexes developed during the late afternoon and evening hours across portions of Yuma and La Paz Counties, likely due to the combination of terrain lift as well as colliding outflows from the storms that developed earlier in the afternoon across portions of Imperial and Riverside Counties.
episodes.173807: Monsoon moisture fueled scattered thunderstorms over southeast California. Many storms produced flash flooding, and a few produced severe weather.
episodes.173808: Monsoon moisture fueled scattered thunderstorms over southern Nevada. A few storms produced flash flooding and severe weather.
episodes.173844: Thunderstorms moved southwest across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and evening.  In the Tucson Metro area, damaging winds downed dozens of power poles and heavy rain resulted in flash flooding. Flash flooding also occurred in the Cochise County community of St. David.
episodes.173868: Thunderstorms in Tooele County brought strong outflow winds.
episodes.173881: Outflow from a decaying thunderstorm produced a wind gust to 59 mph at the Platte Winner Bridge during the early morning hours of August 24th.
episodes.173928: A closed Low over the region shifted over North Idaho and increased instability over the area. The instability mixed with afternoon convection to develop isolated thunderstorms.
episodes.173932: A breach in a berm along Rucker Creek near the northeast edge of Elfrida caused flash flooding in part of town on August 23. Additional rainfall in town and upstream of the breach exacerbated the flooding later that day. Heavy rain well upstream traveled downstream through the breach and flooded more of the town on August 24 and 25. Several homes sustained significant flood damage.
episodes.173955: A very favorable pattern for heavy rain combined with already wet ground conditions led to development of heavy rain and flooding across the area.
episodes.173975: Strong thunderstorms moved over the marine area and produced high winds.
episodes.173981: A very favorable pattern for heavy rain combined with already wet ground conditions led to development of heavy rain and flooding across the area.
episodes.173999: Deep monsoon moisture and increasing shear produce severe thunderstorms and heavy rain over parts of northern Arizona.
episodes.174000: Deep monsoon moisture over northern Arizona brought thunderstorms with heavy rain.
episodes.174062: Weak tornadoes occurred over farm land in the coastal Bend on the 23rd near Driscoll and on the 25th near Edroy. No damage occurred with either tornado.
episodes.178465: A low pressure system spinning over northern Louisiana and southern Arkansas brought several rounds of showers and thunderstorms producing widespread heavy rain to northeast Louisiana through the day August 24th.

A brief EF0 tornado occurred just north of US 98 in West Hattiesburg. Along with multiple videos of a funnel cloud taken along US 98, an employee from a nearby golf course witnessed debris briefly being lofted and another video showed the tornado passing north of a business on 98 Place. No other damage occurred in the area. The tornado appeared the be the result of the intersection of two low level boundaries enhancing shear and very low cloud bases in the exceptionally moisture-rich environment.
